subject: Valence Therapeutics — vulnerability management evidence & owner commitments
messages:
From: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@valencethera.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@valencethera.com
Date: 2027-06-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: VM cadence, SLAs and CVE evidence for SIG/CAIQ questionnaire

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of our security review for the SIG/CAIQ submission we need a concise evidence packet covering Redwood's vulnerability management program. Specifically Valence is asking for: 

- Scan cadence and tooling (IaaS images + app-level scans)
- SLA for critical/high CVE remediation and how exceptions are handled
- A short attestation that CVE ownership and closure timelines are enforceable (for third-party dependencies too)
- Any recent closure logs or a sample runbook we can reference

Can you provide a ZIP with the artifacts or point me to a signed attestation? We have an internal deadline of 2027-06-28 to finalize the SIG answers.

Appreciate it — if you need a formal template I can share one.

-Ravi Shah
Head of Security Operations
Valence Therapeutics
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@valencethera.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VM cadence, SLAs and CVE evidence for SIG/CAIQ questionnaire

Hi Ravi — thanks for the clear list. We're able to provide the artifacts and a short attestation. Quick summary here, full packet attached: 

What we'll send (attached):
- scan index (last 90 days) with scope flags: infra, images, third-party libs
- CVE closure log (sample of recent critical/high closures with ticket links)
- SIG evidence write-up (1-page) describing ownership and exception process

Key SLAs:
- Critical (CVSS >=9): initial triage within 4 hours, mitigation/rollback or compensating control within 72 hours or documented exception
- High (7-8.9): initial triage within 24 hours, remediation within 14 days
- Exceptions: documented in Jira with compensating controls; reviewed weekly by security operations

Owner model: each service has a named owner in our inventory; infra libraries are tracked by Marcus's team with a dependency escalation path. We'll include the runbook snippet showing how an owner is paged and how we map CVEs to owners.

Deliverables are attached as a single ZIP and a one-page signed attestation PDF. Let us know if you need formal signature via DocuSign.

Thanks,

Jasmine Liu
Security & Compliance Partner
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: redwood_vm_scan_index_20270621.csv (CSV), cve-closure-log-VAL-001.pdf (PDF), sig-evidence-summary-VALENCE-2027.pdf (PDF)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-23T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — confirm owners + ready attestation

Jasmine / Markus — looping to confirm the owner list and that the CVE closure log includes third-party library tickets (OSS deps). Items for finalization before we send: 

1) Markus — can you confirm the dependency escalation path is captured in the runbook snippet? Also need a timestamped example where a patch for an external library went through the full process last quarter.
2) I'll sign off on the attestation once we include the names of the owners and the weekly review cadence.
3) Do we want to include the DOC link to our KB article on hotpatching (internal process) or keep that internal-only? Valence usually accepts summary-level controls.

I suggest we redact internal ticket IDs in the sample cve-closure PDF, keep public-facing fields (CVE id, severity, owner, start/end timestamps, resolution type).

-Lauren
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>, Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@valencethera.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: VM cadence, SLAs and CVE evidence for SIG/CAIQ questionnaire

Ravi / team — attaching the finalized packet for Valence. Highlights: 

- Scan cadence: infra weekly authenticated host scans, container image scan on build (every PR) and scheduled composition scans weekly for third-party libs.
- SLA cartoon: critical 72 hours to fix or documented exception; high 14 days; medium tracked in bimonthly backlog.
- Ownership: each service entry in our inventory has an owner; dependency tickets route to the platform team inbox and are assigned within 24 hours.

We included a redacted closure log (cve-closure-log-VAL-001.pdf) showing an external library patch where we coordinated a dependency bump and hotfix; timestamps show triage -> deploy in 6 days (high severity). The sig-evidence-summary PDF includes the attestation language and signature block from our Head of Security.

If Valence needs a notarized or DocuSign-signed artifact, I'm happy to route it — otherwise this packet should satisfy SIG/CAIQ reviewers.

Best,

Markus Klein
Manager, Platform Security Operations
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: redwood_vm_scan_index_20270621.csv, cve-closure-log-VAL-001.pdf, sig-evidence-summary-VALENCE-2027.pdf
